messages:
lena_support: Customer Paywise hit a hard break after our recent model swap. Their webhook consumer parses our structured output and now throws \"Unexpected token [ in JSON at position X\". They say it started right after the model upgrade.

omar_engineering: Can you paste the exact model version and one full example response?

lena_support: Model: rwd-llama4b-2026-02-10 (canary -> prod). Endpoint: POST /v1/generate?mode=structured. request_id=req_abc123. Sample output from the API (customer receives this):

```json
{\"order\": {\"id\": \"ord_9876\", \"line_items\": [[{\"sku\": \"P-001\", \"qty\": 2}]]}}
```

lena_support: Expected \"line_items\" to be a single array of objects, not wrapped in an extra array. Customer parser assumes `array<object>` and fails.

ryan_infra: That double-wrapping looks like the runtime emitted a nested list for arrays with single element, maybe an inference formatting change where sequence-of-sequence was inferred. Did the structured-output post-processor change?

deploy-bot: Canary swap rwd-llama4b-2026-02-10 -> prod at 2026-02-10T03:12:42Z by ops-deploy (canary-level: 100%).

omar_engineering: Repro steps I used: send the same prompt+schema binding that Paywise gave, with Content-Type: application/json and structured schema specifying `line_items: array<object>`. I can repro locally with the canary model.

omar_engineering: Quick workaround: pin the customer route to rwd-llama4b-2026-01-15 (previous variant) until we root-cause. I can add a routing rule that targets customer_id=paywise.

lena_support: Customer is blocked (their webhook consumer rejects any message). They asked for ETA. Can we do the pin today? :pleading_face:

omar_engineering: Yes, we can pin. I'll open a rollback/pin task and push the routing override. Also adding a unit regression test that validates array shapes against simple prompts.

sara_ml: Initial hypothesis: model tokenization/decoder change caused our structured-output serializer to interpret top-level list templates differently for arrays-of-objects. Might be a serialization path with an extra `wrap_sequence` flag flipped during kernel selection for that model build.

ryan_infra: Logs attached from edge that show the model returned a JSON-like string with double brackets; our parser emits it verbatim. We should avoid making caller parsers brittle by fixing output to match schema strictly.

lena_support: I've updated ticket #3421 with repro snippet and customer impact. Notified Paywise that we will pin them and follow up.

omar_engineering: Action items:
- pin Paywise route to rwd-llama4b-2026-01-15 (in progress)
- open eng-ml issue with sample request/response and add regression test (assigned to @sara_ml)
- add a quick lint step in post-processor to collapse nested single-element arrays for array<object> outputs as a defensive hotfix

sara_ml: I'll take the eng-ml issue. If we can't produce a root-cause quick fix, recommend rollout rollback for that model version and block further canary promotion until tests pass.

lena_support: Thanks all — I'll confirm with Paywise once the pin is active. :thumbsup:

ryan_infra: FYI, monitoring alert for structured-output parsing errors spiked from ~0 to 48/min after the canary swap. Keeping an eye on other customers.

omar_engineering: Closing loop: routing pin applied at 2012345710, customer verified webhook ingestion resumed. I'll follow up with a postmortem entry in eng-postmortems and add the regression to the model onboarding checklist.

lena_support: Marking customer ticket as \"workaround applied\" and flagging for SLA credits discussion if needed.

deploy-bot: Rollback/pin automation changed routing for customer:paywise -> rwd-llama4b-2026-01-15 at 2026-03-12T14:15:10Z.

omar_engineering: Thanks team. I'll file the root-cause and link tests.

sara_ml: Ping me if you need sample-generation logs or a dumps file; I pulled a seed that reproduces the nested-array.
